blocks.title: Core concept
blocks.text:
• Physical Properties of Aldehydes/Ketone
  • Methanal (HCHO) is a gas at room temperature.
  • Ethanal (CH₃CHO) is a volatile liquid.
  • The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are higher than those of hydrocarbons and ethers with similar molecular masses.
  • Aldehydes and ketones have lower boiling points compared to alcohols of similar molecular masses.
  • Lower aldehydes and ketones are miscible in water due to their ability to form hydrogen bonds with water molecules.
  • The boiling point order is - Alcohol > Ketone > Aldehydes >Alkane

blocks.title: Question 1
blocks.question:
Q.1 Which of the following exists as a gas at 287K?

a) Formaldehyde

b) Acetaldehyde

c) Propanal

d) Acetone
blocks.answer:
The correct answer is: a) FormaldehydeAt 287 K (~14°C), the boiling points of the given compounds determine their physical state:

Formaldehyde (HCHO): Boiling point is -19°C (below 287 K), so it exists as a gas at this temperature.

Acetaldehyde (CH₃CHO): Boiling point is 20.2°C, so it exists as a liquid at 287 K.

Propanal (CH₃CH₂CHO): Boiling point is 48°C, so it exists as a liquid at 287 K.

Acetone (CH₃COCH₃): Boiling point is 56°C, so it exists as a liquid at 287 K.

Thus, only formaldehyde is a gas at 287 K.

blocks.title: Question 2
blocks.question:
Q,2 Which of the following is the least soluble in water?

a) Methanal

b) Ethanal

c) Propanone

d) Pentanal
blocks.answer:
The correct answer is: d) Pentanal

Solubility in water decreases as the carbon chain length increases because the hydrophobic (nonpolar) alkyl group becomes larger. Among the options, pentanal has the longest chain, making it the least soluble in water.

blocks.title: Question 2
blocks.question:
Q. The compound that will not give iodoform on treatment with alkali and iodine is:

(1) Acetone

(2) Ethanol

(3) Diethyl ketone

(4) Isopropyl alcohol
blocks.answer:
The correct answer is: (3) Diethyl ketone

The iodoform test is positive for compounds with a methyl group attached to a carbonyl group (CH₃C=O) or a structure like CH₃CH(OH).

  • Acetone, ethanol, and isopropyl alcohol all have these groups, so they give a positive iodoform test.
  • Diethyl ketone (CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃) lacks a methyl group directly attached to the carbonyl carbon, so it does not give a positive iodoform test.

blocks.title: Question 1
blocks.question:
Q. Acids have much higher boiling points than isomeric esters because:-

(1) Acids form dimers by H–Bonding

(2) Acids are volatile in steam

(3) Esters are non–volatile

(4) Acids can ionise to give protons in aqueous solution
blocks.answer:
Answer: (1) Acids form dimers by H–Bonding.
Carboxylic acids form dimers due to strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding, significantly increasing their boiling points. Esters lack this extensive hydrogen bonding, resulting in lower boiling points compared to acids.
options: (4) Acids can ionise to give protons in aqueous solution

blocks.title: Question 2
blocks.question:
Q. Which of the following compounds can form intermolecular H–bonds :-

(1) Ethyl acetate

(2) Methyl formate

(3) Acetamide

(4) Acetic anhydride
blocks.answer:
Answer. The compound that can form intermolecular H-bonds is (3) Acetamide

  • Acetamide has an $ NH_2$ group. The hydrogen atoms attached to nitrogen are bonded to a highly electronegative atom (nitrogen), making them capable of forming hydrogen bonds with the lone pair of electrons on the oxygen atom of another acetamide molecule.
The other compounds lack the necessary hydrogen bonding donor (H attached to N, O, or F) or acceptor (lone pair on N, O, or F).

blocks.title: Question
blocks.question:
Q. In the below sequence of reactions, A and B are which of the following?

$\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{CO} \xrightarrow[(\mathrm{HCl})]{\stackrel{\mathrm{NaCN}}{\longrightarrow}} A \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}^{+}} B$

$\text { a) }\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH}) \mathrm{CN},\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH}) \mathrm{COOH}$

$\text { b) }\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH}) \mathrm{CN},\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})_2$

$\text { c) }\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH}) \mathrm{CN},\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{CHCOOH}$

$\text { d) }\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH}) \mathrm{CN},\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$
blocks.answer:
Answer

In this reaction, acetone $(CH_3)_2CO$ reacts with NaCN in the presence of HCl, followed by hydrolysis with $H_3O^+$under heating (Δ).

Reaction sequence:

  • Step 1: Acetone reacts with NaCN and HCl to form a cyanohydrin:
$(CH_3)_2CO + HCN \rightarrow (CH_3)_2C(OH)CN$
The product A is $(CH_3)_2C(OH)CN $(cyanohydrin).
  • Step 2: The cyanohydrin undergoes hydrolysis with $H_3O^+$ and heat to convert the –CN group into –COOH:
$(CH_3)_2C(OH)CN + 2H_2O \rightarrow (CH_3)_2C(OH)COOH$
  • The product B is $(CH_3)_2C(OH)COOH$ ($\alpha$-hydroxycarboxylic acid).
Correct answer:

blocks.title: Question 1
blocks.question:
Q. Arrange the following acids in the correct order of their decreasing acid strength:

(A) Trichloroacetic acid

(B) Trifluoroacetic acid

(C) Formic acid

(D) Acetic acid

Options:

a) B > A > C > D

b) A > B > D > C

c) D > A > B > C

d) B > D > A > C
blocks.answer:
Ans.  a) B > A > C  > D

  • Trifluoroacetic acid (B): The three fluorine atoms are highly electronegative, creating a strong inductive effect, which stabilizes the conjugate base, making it the strongest acid.
  • Trichloroacetic acid (A): Chlorine atoms are less electronegative than fluorine, so the inductive effect is weaker compared to trifluoroacetic acid.
  • Formic acid (C): It lacks halogen atoms but is stronger than acetic acid due to the absence of an electron-donating methyl group.
  • Acetic acid (D): The methyl group donates electrons, reducing the acidity.
